nodes.description: bytes32 state variable holding the keccak256 hash of the secret key that gates the withdrawal.
address state variable set to msg.sender in the constructor; recipient of selfdestruct and gate for extract().
constructor() public: assigns owner = msg.sender at deployment.
withdraw(string key) payable: requires msg.sender == tx.origin, compares keccak256(key) to keyHash and transfers the whole contract balance when msg.value > 0.5 ether.
setup(string key) public: initializes keyHash with keccak256(key) if keyHash is still zero.
new_hash(bytes32 _keyHash) public: initializes keyHash directly if keyHash is still zero.
extract() public: requires msg.sender == owner and then calls selfdestruct(owner).
get_owner() public view: returns the owner address.
fallback function () public payable: accepts plain ether transfers without any logic.
Caller-controlled address used as owner, as an authorization check and as the recipient of the balance transfer.
Transaction origin used in the withdraw authorization check msg.sender == tx.origin.
msg.sender.transfer(address(this).balance): external value transfer of the entire contract balance to an untrusted caller inside withdraw().
selfdestruct(owner): destroys the contract and forwards the whole balance to owner in extract().
string key parameter of withdraw(), hashed with keccak256 for the keyHash comparison.
string key parameter of setup(), hashed with keccak256 and stored into keyHash.
bytes32 _keyHash parameter of new_hash(), assigned directly to keyHash.

edges.reason: constructor assigns owner = msg.sender, writing the owner state variable.
Untrusted msg.sender flows into the privileged owner state variable at deployment.
withdraw authorizes the caller with require(msg.sender == tx.origin), i.e. an untrusted caller-controlled condition.
tx.origin is used as an authorization anchor inside withdraw, tying the transaction origin to the withdrawal path.
withdraw reads keyHash to compare it with keccak256(abi.encodePacked(key)).
setup writes keyHash when it is still zero.
new_hash writes keyHash when it is still zero.
withdraw performs an external value transfer of the entire contract balance to msg.sender before any state is updated.
The recipient of the balance transfer is the untrusted msg.sender.
extract is guarded by require(msg.sender == owner), an untrusted-input authorization check.
extract invokes selfdestruct after passing the owner check.
selfdestruct forwards the remaining contract balance to the owner state variable.
get_owner returns the owner state variable.
The key parameter of withdraw is hashed and compared against keyHash.
The key parameter of setup is hashed and stored into keyHash.
The _keyHash parameter of new_hash is assigned into keyHash.

normalization_plan.reason: The non-core parameter key only exists to feed the keccak256 comparison inside withdraw and has no standalone semantics.
The non-core parameter key is only used to compute the initial keyHash inside setup.
The non-core parameter _keyHash is only used to initialize keyHash inside new_hash.
